acquisition method: chimeric spectra present in classical data-dependent proteomic datasets
alkylation reagent: lysis buffer (50 mM Tris/HCl, pH 7.6, 8 M urea, 10 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphin hydrochloride, 40 mM chloroacetamide, protease and phosphatase inhibitors)
alkylation concentration: lysis buffer (50 mM Tris/HCl, pH 7.6, 8 M urea, 10 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphin hydrochloride, 40 mM chloroacetamide, protease and phosphatase inhibitors)
cleavage agent: trypsin, LysC, ArgC, GluC, AspN, LysN, chymotrypsin
the tonsil sample was subjected to digestion using LysC, ArgC, GluC, AspN, LysN and chymotrypsin
collision energy: Tandem mass spectra were generated for up to 20 precursors by higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) using a normalized collision energy of 25%
fractionation method: The resulting peptides were desalted and concentrated on C18 StageTips (Rappsilber et al, 2007) and fractionated via hSAX off-line chromatography
fragmentation method: Tryptic peptides from the tonsil sample were also analysed on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Mass Spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany) coupled on-line to a nanoflow LC system (UltiMate™ 3000 RSLC Nano System, Thermo Fisher Scientific) using CID, and EThcD/ETD fragmentation
instrument: Q Exactive Plus, Q Exactive HF, Orbitrap Fusion Lumos
Quantitative label-free LC-MS/MS analysis was performed using a Q Exactive Plus mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany)
labeling: We analysed 29 histologically healthy tissue specimen representing major human organs by label-free quantitative proteomics
reduction reagent: lysis buffer (50 mM Tris/HCl, pH 7.6, 8 M urea, 10 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphin hydrochloride, 40 mM chloroacetamide, protease and phosphatase inhibitors)
reduction concentration: lysis buffer (50 mM Tris/HCl, pH 7.6, 8 M urea, 10 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphin hydrochloride, 40 mM chloroacetamide, protease and phosphatase inhibitors)
